title: Control plane: add retention policy schema + validation (feature-flagged)
author: Benji Okafor
description: Summary: This PR introduces the v1 retention policy schema in the control plane, including DB tables, read/write API endpoints, and server-side validation. All functionality is gated behind the feature flag `retention_policies_v1` and is intended to be used by Console + internal automation in follow-up PRs. Motivation: Enterprise security reviews are increasingly asking for tenant-configurable retention and evidence of enforcement. This PR lays the groundwork by making retention policy configuration first-class, validated, and auditable at the control plane layer. Scope: IN: persistence model, API contract, validation/guardrails, and migration notes/backfill behavior for existing tenants. OUT: policy precedence/evaluation (ENG-2912), enforcement jobs (ENG-2920/ENG-2921), and Console UX (ENG-2926/DES-144). Schema overview: New tables: `retention_policies` (one row per org/tenant + environment scope), `retention_policy_rules` (one row per dataset type rule), `retention_policy_audit` (append-only audit events for create/update/delete). A policy has: `scope` (org_id, tenant_id, env, region), `status` (active/disabled), `legal_hold_mode` (inherit/force_on), `created_by`, `updated_by`, and `version` (monotonic integer). Rules are keyed by `dataset_type` (e.g., AUDIT_LOGS, ADMIN_ACTIVITY, REQUEST_METADATA, TELEMETRY_ANALYTICS, OPERATIONAL_LOGS_ELIGIBLE) with `retention_days` and optional `min_days`/`max_days` bounds enforced at validation time. Validation/guardrails: - `retention_days` must be an integer in days (no hours), 1 <= retention_days <= 3650. - Dataset-level guardrails: AUDIT_LOGS min 30 days; ADMIN_ACTIVITY min 30 days; REQUEST_METADATA min 7 days; TELEMETRY_ANALYTICS min 30 days (if enabled); OPERATIONAL_LOGS_ELIGIBLE min 7 days (where applicable). - Disallow "never delete" (infinite retention) unless the caller is an internal service account AND the tenant is in allowlist `RETENTION_ALLOW_INFINITE` (intended for internal testing only). - Legal hold is modeled as an override flag (not a retention_days value). When legal hold is force-enabled, validation allows setting retention_days but records that enforcement must not delete while hold is active (enforcement behavior implemented elsewhere). - Region/env scoping: `env` must be one of prod|staging|dev; `region` must match the control plane region list; for Private deployments where region is customer-defined, region is stored as an opaque string but still validated for length/charset. API endpoints (internal + Console-facing, all behind feature flag): - GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/retention-policy (returns the tenant-scoped policy if present; otherwise returns defaults + "source: default"). - PUT /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/retention-policy (upsert policy + rules; validates and writes audit event). - DELETE /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/retention-policy (soft-disables policy; retains audit trail; does not delete historical rows). - GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/retention-policy/validate (dry-run validation for Console to preflight). Authorization: Writes require `tenant.admin` capability (RBAC), reads require `tenant.viewer` or above. Service-to-service callers can write with `controlplane.retention.write` capability. For all writes, `actor` metadata is recorded (user id / service principal) in `retention_policy_audit`. Migrations/backfill: - Adds new tables with online-safe migrations (no full table rewrite). - No automatic policy row creation during migration to avoid exploding row counts; instead GET endpoint synthesizes defaults when no row exists. - Includes a backfill script (disabled by default) to pre-create default policies for a set of enterprise tenants if needed for rollout monitoring. Rollback: Disabling the feature flag reverts all endpoints to returning 404 ("feature not enabled") and prevents writes; existing tables remain. Observability: Adds structured logs for policy writes (tenant_id, actor_type, changed_dataset_types) and counters `controlplane.retention.policy_write_total{result=...}` and `controlplane.retention.policy_validation_fail_total{reason=...}`. Tests: - Unit tests for schema validation (happy path + invalid bounds + illegal dataset types + infinite retention allowlist). - API contract tests (RBAC, feature-flag behavior, dry-run validate). - Migration test to ensure tables exist and indexes are created as expected. Checklist: [x] Feature flag gates all endpoints [x] RBAC enforced on write paths [x] Audit event written on create/update/disable [x] Unit/integration tests added [x] Migration reviewed for lock safety [x] Docs note added to internal API reference (follow-up will add public docs). Notes for reviewers: The evaluation/precedence logic is intentionally not implemented here; this PR stores policies in a normalized format that the evaluation engine can consume. We can tweak dataset type names now before Console ships if we want cleaner UX labels; the API uses stable enum values, and Console can map to human labels.
commits: controlplane/api: add GET/PUT/DELETE retention policy endpoints (feature-flagged)
controlplane/validation: implement retention policy validator + guardrails
controlplane/auth: enforce RBAC capabilities for retention policy writes
controlplane/audit: append-only retention_policy_audit events on mutations
tests: add validator unit tests + API contract tests
migrations: add indexes + migration safety notes; add optional backfill script
review_conversation: Jordan Lee (review): The schema looks good, but can we avoid encoding precedence rules into storage? E.g., org vs tenant vs env scoping. I want to keep evaluation deterministic and separate. Also, can you add a version field so we can do golden tests later on effective policy diffs?

Benji Okafor (author): Agree on separation. This PR only stores explicit policies; evaluation/precedence will land in ENG-2912. Added `version` (monotonic int) on policy updates and included it in GET responses so eval can cache/stabilize on version.

Kaitlyn Nguyen (review): RBAC: PUT/DELETE should require tenant admin; GET should be viewer+. Also please make sure service principals cannot write unless explicitly granted. Right now looks like any internal service token could call it.

Benji Okafor (author): Updated auth middleware: user token requires `tenant.admin` for writes; service principal requires `controlplane.retention.write`. Added route tests for both paths and for feature-flag disabled behavior.

Marcus Lin (review): Guardrails: minimums per dataset type should be enforced server-side (not just Console). Also, disallow "infinite" unless explicitly allowlisted; we've been burned by accidental never-delete toggles in other systems.

Benji Okafor (author): Implemented per-dataset minimums and a hard disallow of infinite retention by default. Infinite is only allowed for internal service principals and only when tenant is in `RETENTION_ALLOW_INFINITE` allowlist (intended for dev/testing). Added explicit validation reasons to metrics/logs.

Michael Nguyen (review): Migration safety: do we have any risk of long locks on the main control plane DB? Please ensure indexes are created concurrently / with our safe migration tool, and avoid default values that rewrite existing tables.

Benji Okafor (author): Migration only creates new tables; no rewrite. Index creation uses our `SAFE_INDEX` helper which maps to concurrent index creation for Postgres. Added a note in migration header + ran `db-migration-safety` check in CI.

Ethan Park (review): Nice. One thing: do we want GET to return 404 when no policy exists, or return defaults? For Console UX, returning defaults is easier, but we should label the source. Also ensure audit events are append-only and immutable.

Benji Okafor (author): Implemented GET to synthesize defaults when no row exists, returning `source=default` and `policy_id=null`. Audit events are append-only; we never update existing audit rows (only insert).
Jordan Lee (follow-up): Please add a dry-run validate endpoint for Console to show errors inline without writing anything, and include structured validation errors (dataset_type + reason).
Benji Okafor (author): Added GET /retention-policy/validate which runs the validator and returns normalized errors. Console can call it pre-submit. Included tests.
Marcus Lin (approval): Approved. Please coordinate with ENG-2934 on legal hold semantics; current modeling seems compatible.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (approval): Approved after RBAC fixes.
Ethan Park (approval): Approved; ship behind flag and stage rollout with canary tenants.
release_notes: Internal: Introduce retention policy configuration schema + validation in control plane (feature-flagged). No customer-visible behavior change until Console + enforcement are enabled.
